previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, and atrial flutter was admitted for recurrent substernal chest pain following hemodialysis. The pain was attributed to fluid shifts affecting her cardiac physiology. During the admission, she experienced an acute respiratory failure and PEA arrest requiring CPR, intubation, and ICU care. She recovered and was extubated, but developed musculoskeletal chest pain from chest compressions. An echo confirmed severe LVH with mild outflow obstruction, and a head CT showed small vessel ischemic disease and a nonspecific frontal lesion. Her INR was elevated at discharge, so warfarin was held. She was transitioned to a rehab facility for strength recovery with optimized medications, including increased metoprolol, addition of lisinopril, and dialysis modifications to limit fluid removal and include pre-treatment beta blockade.

Acute on Chronic Diastolic Heart Failure: The patient's most 
recent echocardiogram from ___ showed a preserved ejection

onset shortness of breath at home.  The precipitant for this 
event is unclear.  She had no evidence of ischemia on her EKG.  
She had three sets of negative cardiac enzymes.  She reported no 
dietary or medication non-compliance. She did not miss any 
dialysis sessions. In the emegency room she transiently required 
CPAP and was started on a nitroglycerin drip.  Her blood 
pressure was aggressively treated.  She was weaned off the 
nitroglycerin drip and received hemodialysis for volume control 
with good effect.  She was quickly weaned off oxygen.  On 
hospital day two she was breathing comfortably off oxygen and 
ambulating without assistance.  No changes were made to her 
outpatient medication regimen. She was discharged with close 
follow up with her primary care physician.  

Hypertension: The patient's blood pressures grossly elevated on 
presentation to the emergency room.  She initially required a 
nitroglycerin drip and received hemodialysis.  She was started 
back on her home regimen with good blood pressure control.  

Diabetes: The patient is on insulin at home.  Per her most 
recent discharge summary she was on a regimen which includes NPH 
as well as standing novolog.  During this admission the patient 
reported that she does not take long acting insulin and only 
takes novolog 4 mg BID at home.  The patient was advised to 
discuss this issue with her primary care physician at her follow 
up appointment.
